root_cause.text: The function `unlink_nv12_plane()` was being called after `plane_atomic_check()` had already computed the new plane state, causing it to clobber state that had just been set up, because a previous visibility check that prevented this clobbering was removed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the `unlink_nv12_plane()` call to `intel_plane_set_invisible()` which is invoked before `plane_atomic_check()` computes the new plane state. The commit message explicitly states: "unlink_nv12_plane() will clobber parts of the plane state potentially already set up by plane_atomic_check(), so we must make sure not to call the two in the wrong order" and "This used to work on account of unlink_nv12_plane() skipping the state clearing based on the plane visibility. But I removed that check, thinking it was an impossible situation." The patch also adds an early return guard `if (!plane_state->planar_linked_plane) return;` to prevent unnecessary operations when there is no linked plane to unlink.

intent_record.intent_summary: Unlink NV12 plane associations before clearing plane visibility state to prevent dangling references in multi-plane NV12 configurations.
intent_record.what: Added a forward declaration for `unlink_nv12_plane()` function and inserted a call to `unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state)` at the beginning of the `intel_plane_set_invisible()` function, before the existing bitwise AND operations that clear plane state flags.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that when a plane is marked invisible, any NV12 plane linkage is explicitly unlinked before the plane's visibility and scaling state are cleared from the CRTC state. This prevents potential issues where linked NV12 planes might retain stale references or relationships after the primary plane becomes invisible.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add early return guard to skip unnecessary unlink operations when planar_linked_plane is already NULL.
intent_record.what: Added a null check guard clause at the beginning of unlink_nv12_plane() that returns early if plane_state->planar_linked_plane is NULL, before attempting to set it to NULL.
intent_record.how: This prevents unnecessary processing when planar_linked_plane is already NULL. Without this check, the function would proceed to execute the remaining logic (the NULL assignment and conditional block) even when there is no linked plane to unlink, which is redundant and potentially unsafe if subsequent operations depend on a valid state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant null check by relying on unlink_nv12_plane() to handle all cases internally.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional check `if (plane_state->planar_linked_plane)` before calling `unlink_nv12_plane(crtc_state, plane_state)`, making the function call unconditional.
intent_record.how: The function `unlink_nv12_plane()` will now be invoked for every plane in the loop regardless of whether `planar_linked_plane` is set. This means planes without linked planes will also go through the unlinking logic, which likely handles the null/unset case internally.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `unlink_nv12_plane()` (lines 269-279) unconditionally modifies `crtc_state->nv12_planes` at line 273 by clearing the plane's bit. According to the vulnerability root cause, this function was being called after `plane_atomic_check()` had already computed the new plane state, causing it to clobber state that had just been set up. The commit message indicates that a previous visibility check that prevented this clobbering was removed. The function body shows no conditional check (such as a visibility guard) before performing the state modifications - it simply unconditionally clears the nv12_planes bitmask and other state fields. This is the vulnerable construct: the function modifies plane state without the protective visibility check that should prevent it from clobbering previously computed state.
